Browser chat URLs are stored in SQLite chats.chat_url column (auto-migrated). Saved after every scraper response via save_chat_url(). Retrieved via get_chat_url() to navigate scraper back to correct conversation instead of opening fresh empty chat.

When scraper_service.chat() receives a chat_id that differs from self.active_chat_id and no chat_url is provided, it opens a brand new browser chat via engine.new_chat() — causing messages to be sent into empty conversations. Fix: always pass chat_url when calling scraper_service.chat() for non-active chats.

Two consolidation endpoints: POST /api/memory/consolidate (API mode, uses service.chat with parent_id threading) and POST /api/memory/consolidate-scraper (scraper mode, uses scraper_service.chat with chat_url navigation). Both parse JSON response and apply add/delete operations to Memory.json and Protected.json.

SkillParser._hold_start() in engine/skills.py failed to hold partial tags split across SSE streaming chunks when attributes were mid-stream. The check `any(tag.startswith(partial))` only matched when partial was shorter than the tag name; once attributes arrived (e.g. 'view_file path="/home/...'), no known tag started with that string. semantic.key: phantom_bot regex rewriter double prefix bug
semantic.value: Regex rewriter (app.py ~L125) rewrites absolute paths like href='/static/...' by prepending url_prefix. When url_for already generated prefixed paths (via SCRIPT_NAME), the regex added another prefix, breaking CSS loads. Fix: exclude paths already starting with url_prefix by adjusting regex pattern to r'((?:href|action|src)\s*=\s*")(/(?!/|{url_prefix.lstrip('/')}/))'.

Index page (/ or /panel/) executes ~6 parallel MongoDB count queries on load. When Atlas cold-start delays first connection, all queries hang and proxy (aiohttp) times out (502). Not yet fixed; potential solutions: reduce query count, add timeout handling, or warm-up connection before request.

semantic.key: phantom_bot JS hardcoded path fix pattern
semantic.value: To fix JS files with hardcoded absolute paths under a url_prefix: 1) Pass url_prefix to template via render_template('...', url_prefix=url_prefix or ''). 2) In template before script tag, set window.URL_PREFIX = '{{ url_prefix }}'. 3) In JS, const P = window.URL_PREFIX || '' and prepend P to all absolute URL strings.

semantic.key: Sable memory search hybrid scoring formula
semantic.value: MemorySearcher uses hybrid score: 0.7*vector_similarity + 0.3*keyword_coverage. Keyword coverage = |query_tokens ∩ entry_tokens| / |query_tokens|. Protected entries get +0.15 boost. This blend significantly lowers scores vs pure cosine similarity — thresholds must be calibrated for hybrid, not raw vector scores.

test/memory_benchmark.py converted from sentence-transformers to fastembed TextEmbedding backend on 2026-07-27. Original used SentenceTransformer with trust_remote_code and manual query/doc prefixes; new version uses FastEmbed which handles prefixes internally. MODEL_REGISTRY simplified to short_name -> model_id mapping. Eliminates tokenizers version conflict (transformers<=0.23.0 vs fastembed needing 0.23.1).

test/test_embedding.py --live flag pulls last 50 user prompts from sable.db, runs them against real Brain/Memory.json entries, displays raw scores per result with ★ marker for scores >= 0.6, and outputs score distribution (min/p25/median/p75/max) with suggested threshold as midpoint between p25 and median. Supports --top-k and --model flags. Runs all 8 models by default when no --model specified.

calibrate_thresholds.py in Sable root measures each model's TP/FP score separation against 12 relevant queries (mapped to specific memory keys) and 8 irrelevant queries (including hard tech negatives). Recommends threshold as midpoint between FP ceiling and TP floor when cleanly separable. Run via uv run python calibrate_thresholds.py. Used to produce the 2026-07-27 MODEL_THRESHOLDS calibration.

semantic.key: Sable per-model threshold editor in settings

Backend stores overrides as model_thresholds dict in memory_search_settings.json. Searcher.get_threshold(model) checks custom override first, falls back to MODEL_THRESHOLDS. Chats table has a 'mode' column ('api' or 'scraper') auto-migrated on startup. Mode is locked on first message via ensure_chat(mode=current_mode). get_chat_mode(chat_id) retrieves it. /api/chat blocks sends when current global scraper_enabled state mismatches the chat's locked mode, returning error: 'This chat was created in {mode} mode. Switch back to {mode} mode or start a new chat.' Existing chats without mode get locked on next interaction.

semantic.key: Sable ONNX Runtime memory arena fix
semantic.value: fastembed's ONNX Runtime pre-allocates a massive CPU memory arena by default — 4.2GB RSS for a 90MB embedding model (snowflake-arctic-embed-xs), peaking at 6.87GB VmPeak. Fix: pass enable_cpu_mem_arena=False to TextEmbedding() in engine/memory_search.py _ensure_model(). fastembed exposes this via EXPOSED_SESSION_OPTIONS in common/onnx_model.py. After fix: 52MB RSS, 113MB VmPeak. Single anonymous mmap of 4192MB was the arena.

episodic.key: ONNX 4GB memory arena diagnosed and fixed 2026-07-28
episodic.value: Sable uvicorn process growing to 7-8GB. Diagnosed via /proc/PID/smaps_rollup (4.29GB RSS, 6.87GB VmPeak) and /proc/PID/maps (single 4192MB anonymous mmap). Root cause: ONNX Runtime enable_cpu_mem_arena=True default in fastembed. One-line fix: enable_cpu_mem_arena=False in TextEmbedding() constructor. Result: 4290MB → 52MB RSS (98.8% reduction). Stabilized immediately — not a slow leak but a massive upfront allocation.

procedural.value: When scraper messages fail silently (empty answer, no error), check: 1) Is chat_url being passed to scraper_service.chat()? Without it, mismatched chat_id triggers new_chat() instead of navigating to existing conversation. 2) Check stream_events logic around line 605 in engine/scraper.py where chat_id != self.active_chat_id branches. 3) Verify browser tab is alive via _is_browser_alive() check.

When phantom_bot is reported broken: 1) Check git log/status for uncommitted changes or recent bad commits. 2) Inspect bot/main.py entry point and config.py for import/config errors. 3) Verify .env exists and has required vars. 4) Try running with uv run python -m bot.main to catch runtime errors. 5) Check if dependencies need uv sync.

When Sable skill tags fail intermittently: 1) Check _hold_start() logic for split-tag handling — verify both tag.startswith(partial) AND partial.startswith(tag) checks exist. 2) Test with simulated multi-chunk streaming using standalone script (not inline python -c which gets intercepted by the live parser). 3) Check for undefined variables in handlers (grep for suspicious names). 4) Verify syntax with py_compile before declaring fix. 5) NEVER restart sable during active session.

To deploy phantom_bot with webhook on Render: Set env vars IS_LOCAL=False, USE_WEBHOOK=True, WEBHOOK_URL=https://app-name.onrender.com, WEBHOOK_PORT=8443 (or Render-assigned port). Render auto-provisions SSL on .onrender.com. Free tier caveat: spins down after inactivity, Telegram webhooks don't count as keep-alive activity — use paid tier or external uptime pinger. Bot token is used as webhook URL path automatically.

procedural.key: Debugging phantom_bot cloudflare tunnel URL-prefix issues
procedural.value: When phantom_bot pages fail under a URL prefix (e.g., /panel), check: 1) JS files for hardcoded absolute paths (fetch, location.href) that lack prefix — inject url_prefix via template. 2) Server-side routes that render templates must pass url_prefix to enable JS prefixing. 3) Regex rewriter (for HTML attrs) must avoid double-prefixing paths already generated by url_for. 4) Homepage slowness: MongoDB Atlas cold-start can cause 502 if index route makes many parallel queries; consider connection warming or query reduction.

procedural.key: Calibrating memory search thresholds for new models
procedural.value: When adding or changing embedding models in Sable: 1) Add model to MODEL_THRESHOLDS with a placeholder value. 2) Run calibrate_thresholds.py to measure real TP/FP score separation. 3) Update threshold to recommended value. 4) Verify with test/test_embedding.py --live --model <name> against real prompts. Do NOT reuse thresholds from other models or pure-vector benchmarks — hybrid scoring shifts all distributions.

procedural.key: Running live threshold analysis across all models
procedural.value: To compare all models against real usage: cd /home/sifat/hdd/projects/Sable && uv run python test/test_embedding.py --live --top-k 5. Outputs per-prompt raw scores and threshold suggestion for each of 8 models. Use --model X to isolate one. Note: with small memory stores (<50 entries), even irrelevant queries score high — separation improves as store grows.

procedural.key: Diagnosing memory injection failures in Sable
procedural.value: When memory injection appears to never trigger: 1) Run test/test_memory_injection.py with recent prompts to see raw hybrid scores vs threshold. 2) If all scores are below threshold, run test/test_hybrid_threshold.py to recalibrate — hybrid scoring (0.7v+0.3k) produces different distributions than pure cosine. 3) Check server.py /api/chat endpoint lines ~1206-1225 for silent exception swallowing. 4) Verify per-chat dedup isn't over-filtering by checking SQLite chats.memory_keys column. 5) After changing thresholds, restart server or use per-model threshold editor in settings to apply without restart.

When modifying Sable DB helper functions to access new columns: always check that the SELECT statement explicitly includes the column name before accessing via row["col"]. SQLite Row objects only contain columns listed in SELECT — accessing an unlisted column raises IndexError/KeyError causing 500s. Grep for the SELECT query when extending existing functions.

procedural.key: Diagnosing Python process memory bloat on Linux
procedural.value: When a Python process uses excessive RAM: 1) grep VmRSS/VmPeak /proc/PID/status for overview. 2) cat /proc/PID/smaps_rollup for Rss/Pss/AnonHugePages breakdown. 3) Parse /proc/PID/maps to find large anonymous mappings (>100MB) — single huge anon mmaps indicate allocator arenas (ONNX, numpy, jemalloc). 4) Compare RSS vs VmPeak: big gap means allocation-then-free pattern (arena pre-allocation). 5) Check loaded .so files via grep on maps to identify the library. 6) For ONNX specifically: disable enable_cpu_mem_arena in SessionOptions.
